newsitem.title: INDIA: India's bank stocks climb after RBI credit policy.
newsitem.headline: India's bank stocks climb after RBI credit policy.

text.p: Indian bank shares rose on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday as investors bought on the central bank's market-friendly credit policy announced earlier this week, traders said.
Shares of largest commercial bank State Bank of India climbed 7.50 rupees, or 2.6 percent, to 294.50 in large volumes.
Oriental Bank of Commerce shares rose 2.50 rupees, or 3.4 percent, to 75 and HDFC Bank gained 2.75 rupees, or 5.3 percent, to 54.75.

"The policy doesn't add directly to banks' bottomlines but the fact that they have been giveN much more operational freedom is a big plus point, especially for the frontline banks," said a banking analyst at a foreign brokerage.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) loosened its credit policy for the first six months of 1997/98 (April-March) to bring down interest rates and keep economic growth on track while containing inflation.
RBI governor Chakravarty Rangarajan said a number of steps had been taken in the credit policy to improve the credit delivery system.
"We have given greater autonomy to banks to determine working capital limits for borrowers and also eased norms on consortium lending," he said.
